docs.title: Overwatch
docs.text:
Overwatch assesses software requirements for correctness. Point it at a requirements file, name a requirement, and it returns a verdict on whether that requirement conforms to EARS — the Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax — along with the matched pattern and a short rationale.

Under the hood, the owatch CLI sends the requirement to the Overwatch REST API, which asks a foundation model (via Amazon Bedrock, in-region in eu-west-2) to judge it against the five EARS patterns.

docs.title: Verdicts
docs.text: Verdict Meaning Compliant The requirement matches one of the five EARS patterns; matched_pattern names which. Non-Compliant It is a requirement, but fits no EARS pattern. Indeterminate It cannot be judged as a requirement at all — empty, a question, a fragment.

docs.title: The five EARS patterns
docs.text: Pattern Shape Ubiquitous The <system> shall <response>. Event-driven When <trigger>, the <system> shall <response>. State-driven While <state>, the <system> shall <response>. Unwanted behaviour If <condition>, then the <system> shall <response>. Optional feature Where <feature>, the <system> shall <response>.

Project status

Overwatch is in early development. Access currently requires credentials provisioned by the operator of an Overwatch deployment — see Getting started.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
owatch is configured entirely through environment variables — there are no config files and no URL flags:

Variable What it is OWATCH_API_URL Base URL of the Overwatch REST API deployment. COGNITO_CLIENT_ID Client ID of the deployment's Cognito user pool app client. AWS_REGION Region the Cognito pool lives in (e.g. eu-west-2). OWATCH_REFRESH_TOKEN Your Cognito refresh token; exchanged for an access token on every run.

All four come from the operator of the Overwatch deployment you're using. A missing variable fails fast with an error naming it.

Developing Overwatch itself?

A deployed dev stack provides all four: run make login once, then eval "$(make export-envvars)" in your shell.

docs.title: The requirements file
docs.text:
Requirements live in a YAML file: a list of entries, each with a free-form id and the requirement text.

- id: REQ_001
  requirement: When a user submits a requirement, the Overwatch REST API shall return an assessment.
- id: REQ_002
  requirement: The system should probably be fast.

IDs must be non-empty and contain only letters, digits, _ or -, so they stay unambiguous in YAML, logs, and error messages.

docs.title: Assessing a requirement
docs.text:
Name the requirement to assess with -r and pass the file:

owatch assess -r REQ_001 ./requirements.yaml

On success the CLI prints the name of a time-stamped assessment file it has written to the current directory:

assessment_20260826_155425_767111.yaml

which contains the result:

- id: REQ_001
  ears_assessment: Compliant
  matched_pattern: Event-driven
  rationale: The requirement follows the When <trigger>, the <system> shall <response> shape.

See Home for what the verdicts and patterns mean, and the CLI reference for every command and flag.

docs.title: When it fails
docs.text:
• OWATCH_API_URL is not set (or any of the other three) — the environment isn't configured; see Configuration.
  • unknown command "./requirements.yaml" — the assess subcommand was omitted: it's owatch assess -r ... <file>, not owatch -r ....
  • authenticating: ... — the refresh token has expired or the Cognito details are wrong; obtain fresh credentials from your operator.
  • A 500 from the API — the failure is server-side (the model call itself, or its configuration); nothing the CLI flags can fix. Report it to your operator.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Overwatch ships as a single static binary. Prebuilt archives for Linux, macOS, and Windows are published on the releases page.

docs.title: Linux and macOS
docs.text:
Pick the latest version from the releases page, then substitute it and your platform below. Archives are named owatch_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz — linux or darwin, amd64 or arm64 (Apple Silicon is darwin_arm64).

VERSION=0.1.0
PLATFORM=linux_amd64

curl -LO "https://github.com/the-common-developers/owatch-releases/releases/download/v${VERSION}/owatch_${VERSION}_${PLATFORM}.tar.gz"
tar -xzf "owatch_${VERSION}_${PLATFORM}.tar.gz"
sudo install owatch /usr/local/bin/

To verify the download, every release includes a checksums.txt:

curl -LO "https://github.com/the-common-developers/owatch-releases/releases/download/v${VERSION}/checksums.txt"
sha256sum --check --ignore-missing checksums.txt

(macOS ships shasum instead: shasum -a 256 --check --ignore-missing checksums.txt.)

docs.title: Windows
docs.text: Download owatch_<version>_windows_amd64.zip from the releases page, extract owatch.exe, and place it somewhere on your PATH.

docs.title: Verify the install
docs.text:
owatch --version

This prints the release version, e.g. owatch version 0.1.0.

docs.title: owatch assess
docs.text:
Assess a single requirement from a requirements file.

owatch assess <requirements-file> [flags]

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
-h, --help                 help for assess
  -o, --output-dir string    directory the assessment file is written into (default "assessments")
  -r, --requirement string   id of the requirement to assess
